### Added
- The `global.*` input contract, in both charts, with backward-compatible fallbacks — **an installation that sets none of the new keys renders byte-identically** (the connectivity golden check pins this). Upstreamed from the standalone chart's vanilla-defaults work so the generated standalone templates need no patches:
  - `global.domain`: the one hostname input. Public hostnames derive from it by convention (`muster.`, `agentgateway.`, `kagent.<domain>`), each still overridable next to its route (`ingress.hostnames`, `kagent.uiRoute.hostname`, `kagent.controllerRoute.hostname`). The kagent route guards now accept a derived hostname: with `global.domain` set, `kagent.uiRoute.hostname` is optional.
  - `global.identity` (`issuerUrl`, `clientId`, `existingSecret`): the platform's one login provider. The kagent JWT policy defaults its `issuer` from `global.identity.issuerUrl`; the render fails when muster's own `muster.muster.oauth.server.*` keys disagree with a set `global.identity` (both sides set and different — installs that ignore `global.identity` are untouched).
  - `global.gatewayApi.parentRefs`: the public Gateway every umbrella-owned route attaches to when neither its own `parentRefs`/`parentRef` override nor the chart-owned edge names one. The all-modes `ingress.parentRefs` requirement is now satisfied by any of the three sources; the failure message names them all.
  - `global.observability.metrics.serviceMonitor` (`enabled` default `true`, `interval`, `labels`): gates the monitor objects the connectivity chart renders — the kagent controller ServiceMonitor (+ its metrics Service) and the CNPG Cluster's built-in PodMonitor — for clusters without the `monitoring.coreos.com` CRDs. The per-component `kagent.serviceMonitor.*` keys keep working underneath; `interval`/`labels` fall back to them.
  - `global.observability.traces.otlp` (`endpoint`, `protocol`, `headers`): OTEL exporter env for the agentgateway data plane. An empty endpoint renders nothing and `gateway.parameters.dataPlaneEnv` applies unchanged; a set endpoint wins over same-named entries in that list, so no duplicate env names.
- `ingress.httpRoute.timeouts` (default `{}`): portable Gateway API rule timeouts on the umbrella-owned routes (muster `/`, agentgateway `/mcp`, kagent UI and public controller routes). `request: "0s"` asks the implementation to disable the request timeout so MCP/SSE streams stay open without the Envoy-specific `ingress.backendTrafficPolicy`.
- `gatewayApi.gateway.create` (default `false`, with `tls.secretName` and `serviceType`): edge mode — the chart-owned agentgateway data-plane Gateway is also the public edge. It grows an HTTPS `:443` listener for `*.<global.domain>` (`allowedRoutes` from all namespaces), the umbrella-owned public routes pin themselves to that listener via `sectionName` (the plaintext `:8080` listener never serves public hostnames through the edge's LoadBalancer Service), the layer-1 routes that would forward a front Gateway to the agentgateway Service are suppressed (the data plane must not proxy to itself, and their `BackendTrafficPolicy` with them), the data-plane Service type switches to `gatewayApi.gateway.serviceType`, and the data-plane NetworkPolicy (both flavors) admits world traffic on 443 only. Guards require the agentgateway mode, the certificate Secret and `global.domain`. **The fleet never sets this** — it exists for standalone installs (kind, vanilla clusters) without a front Gateway. Known accepted quirk, documented in the muster route template: in edge mode the hostname-specific muster `/` route also serves `muster.<domain>/mcp` directly (hostname precedence), so the MCP path degrades to muster-direct semantics on that hostname; behavioral acceptance is owned by the standalone kind smoke.
### Changed
- The CNPG `Cluster` carries `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep`: the database outlives the release, so an uninstall or a `postgres.enabled` flip no longer drops the platform's data. Removing the database now takes an explicit `kubectl delete cluster` after the release change.
- The CNPG Cluster's `inheritedMetadata` labels and `monitoring` block are gated on `global.observability.metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled` (default `true` — no installation needs to act), and the labels come from `global.observability.metrics.serviceMonitor.labels`, defaulting to the Giant Swarm tenant label as before.
### Fixed
- The CNPG cluster CiliumNetworkPolicy (`<clusterName>-cluster`: replication egress, controller ingress) is gated on `postgres.enabled`. It used to render for every kagent install under the cilium flavor, naming a Postgres cluster that does not exist.
- The kagent `uiRoute`/`controllerRoute` `parentRef` overrides fail the render when `.name` is set without `.namespace` — the Gateway API CRD rejects an empty namespace, which used to break the route silently after install.
